tests.experiment: Per-token sharpness of RL step-100 finished answers relative to the cued base: share of step-100 plain finished answers whose mean_logprob exceeds the median mean_logprob of the cued base's finished answers, MATH-500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
tests.recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (R, reference) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (X). In each file keep rows with sample == 0; if a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. Keep problem_index values present in both files (set S). In each file, finished rows = rows in S with cap_hit false (if cap_hit is missing, finished only if finish_reason == 'stop'). Drop rows whose mean_logprob field is missing, null or non-finite. Let M = median of mean_logprob over R's finished rows (even count: mean of the two middle values). Statistic: (number of X finished rows with mean_logprob strictly greater than M) / (number of X finished rows). Ties with M count as not greater. Cap-hit rows are excluded from both files.
tests.note: Files: s3 r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (R) and r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (X), fetched to runs/theory-tests/duel-r4-m10t2/. Rows have sample, problem_index, cap_hit (bool), finish_reason, mean_logprob. Main (literal): S = problem_index sets intersected after sample==0 and first-occurrence dedup; finished/valid filters applied per file independently, so R's median and X's denominator can use different problems. Alt: paired reading, only problems finished with finite mean_logprob in both files. Ties with M count as not greater. refuted_by is null so refuted_by_met is always false. Possible issues: mean_logprob is computed over the whole generation including any prefill/cue tokens differences between the F (cued, prefill_ids present) and P (plain) cells, so R vs X are not token-for-token comparable; if cap_hit is a non-bool string the script would treat it as not finished.

tests.experiment: Where step 400's median per-token log-prob on finished answers lies between the cued base and step 2,800, plain prompt for RL checkpoints, MATH-500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
tests.recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (R), s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_math500.jsonl (M) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (E). In each file keep rows with sample == 0; if a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. Keep problem_index values present in all three files (set S). In each file, finished rows = rows in S with cap_hit false (if cap_hit is missing, finished only if finish_reason == 'stop'). Drop rows whose mean_logprob is missing, null or non-finite. med_X = median of mean_logprob over X's finished rows (even count: mean of the two middle values). Statistic: (med_M - med_R) / (med_E - med_R). If med_E - med_R equals 0, report undefined.
tests.note: Files: R = r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl, M = r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_math500.jsonl, E = r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl. S = problems present (sample==0, first occurrence) in all three files; each median taken over that file's finished rows with finite mean_logprob in S independently (main). Alt: medians over problems finished with finite mean_logprob in all three files. If med_E == med_R the script reports not_computable 'undefined' as the recipe says. Ratio is sensitive to small denominators if med_E is close to med_R; values outside [0,1] are reported as is.
